workstream: W-50 — no inert capability is presented as a control (IA-R8, T-6)
what_this_is: Catalog keys that no product source names on an executable line. Nothing can consult a key that appears nowhere, so every one of these is a control that changes nothing — 'revocation theatre' (T-6). Since W-10 the grid projects the whole catalog, which is how they became visible controls.
why_json_and_not_typescript: The enforcement scan reads .ts/.tsx under web/app, web/lib, web/components and web/scripts. Writing these keys as TypeScript literals in web/lib would give every one of them an enforcement site and make the artifact falsify the scan that produces it. A .json file is invisible to that walk, so the list can be imported at runtime without becoming evidence for itself.
not_a_deletion: Listing a key here removes it from the operator's *controls*, not from the catalog. Deleting the catalog rows is OD-3 and belongs to the operator; presenting them honestly until then does not.
locked_by: web/tests/access/permissionEnforcementTruth.test.ts — this list must equal a fresh derivation from the tree, in both directions. A key that gains its first enforcement site fails until it is removed here; a key that loses its last one fails until it is added.
conservative_direction: The scan counts a key as enforced if any product source names it, which over-counts (a helper may mention a key no route reaches). So this list is a floor: everything on it is certainly inert, and keys not on it may still be inert. It can never accuse an enforced key.
